original_test_intent: Inject the specified USB RAM fault across the required RAM1~N targets, verify the intended corrected or reset behavior with target-specific durable evidence, and prove the USB controller, ports and attached devices recover.
original_method: Enumerate valid USB targets; map every reported RAM target to socket, controller, instance, errortarget, port and device; resolve severity/reset policy and command-line formatting; capture raw BIOS/log/device baselines; inject one approved target once under OOB capture; correlate fresh source fields and reset; validate controller/device recovery; repeat only for an approved coverage matrix with restoration between targets.
manual_activity: The FAE defines RAM1~N, maps every valid USB target, resolves the corrected-versus-reset contract and command syntax, performs serialized injections and restores controller/device state.
required_inputs: Definition of USB RAM1~N and complete required controller/instance/target/port/device coverage
Full listvalidusb output and immutable physical mapping for socket0 instance1 target1 and any N targets
Vendor-correct one-line or continued command syntax and semantics of usbsata errortype usb
Decision on correctable Criteria versus immediate reset, including exact severity/source fields
Rationale for SATA RAS Support in USB coverage and USB ECC SMI behavior
Supported OS, timeouts, boot/input/storage/management-device recovery, aborts and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated SUT with independent console that is not the targeted USB device or port
Inventory boot media, input devices, USB NIC/BMC dependencies and active storage before selecting a target
Inject one mapped target once and require full device/controller recovery before any next target
Abort on ambiguous enumeration, wrong device, unexpected severity/reset, boot failure, device loss, filesystem impact or stale/missing evidence
No automatic retry or blind RAM1~N loop; restore BIOS/HDT/controller state per target
agent_execution_scope: Validate range definition, mapping, command syntax, severity/reset oracle and recovery matrix
Collect read-only enumeration, topology, raw settings, OOB timeline, RAS/SEL and USB controller/device health
Do not join command lines by assumption, select targets, change BIOS/HDT, inject, reset, repeat, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve source conflicts and approve target matrix
Approve exact syntax, severity/reset and persistent evidence
Restore state and issue per-target verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A generic USB/fatal/error grep cannot show which listvalidusb entry was hit, whether RAM1~N coverage was completed or why a correctable case reset.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a reviewed physical mapping and vendor-correct invocation for one target, capture reset and source-specific evidence, validate every USB dependency, then separately authorize additional N targets.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidusb, usbsata, errortype usb, socket0, instance1, errortarget1, immediate reset, SATA RAS, USB ECC SMI, three OS families and 15/10-minute values remain preserved as disputed inputs.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a physical target matrix one device at a time with exact tuple attribution, deterministic reset policy and complete USB dependency recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds range coverage, command parsing decision, severity reconciliation, target identity, safety exclusions, persistent evidence and per-target rollback.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single hard-coded RAM1 tuple cannot prove RAM1~N, and a generic log cannot prove target or recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong selection may reset the host, remove boot/input/network/storage devices or make the management path unavailable.

project_override_considerations: If listvalidusb exposes fewer or differently numbered RAM targets, preserve the source range and record explicit applicability rather than inventing indices. Never target a boot, management or active-storage USB function without an approved isolated substitute.
expected_evidence: Full valid-USB enumeration with controller/port/device and RAM1~N mapping
Approved command syntax, tuple and corrected-versus-reset policy plus raw settings baseline
Separate exact transcript and OOB timeline per authorized target
Recovered USB controller, port, device enumeration and relevant input/network/storage transaction health
Per-target restoration diff and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: RAM1~N scope conflicts with a single RAM1/instance1/target1 command. The Criteria says correctable tool PASS while Procedure mandates immediate reset; errortype usb does not expose severity. The command is split without an explicit continuation, SATA RAS relevance is unexplained, and target/time/recovery criteria are incomplete.

blocked_analysis.analysis: USB RAS injection and the literal tuple are identifiable. Engineering can resolve the range, syntax and acceptance conflicts, so static review completes while execution remains gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 87 Wistron-System RAS-00807-V002: define USB RAM1~N and the complete listvalidusb controller/instance/target/port/device matrix; approve vendor-correct command joining and usbsata errortype usb semantics; reconcile correctable Criteria with immediate reset; explain SATA RAS and USB ECC SMI relevance; specify target-specific fresh RAS/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, OS/reset/boot timeouts, safe-device exclusions, per-target recovery, aborts and restoration.

review_improvement: Converts an ambiguous range label and hard-coded target into a physical per-device coverage matrix while exposing the severity/reset and command-format contradictions.
independent_technical_reasoning: The list command exists because instance and target values are platform-dependent; the literal 1/1 tuple therefore cannot represent RAM1~N without a mapping. A command broken across lines may execute only its first half if copied literally. More importantly, a correctable acceptance rule conflicts with an immediate reset, so evidence and recovery cannot be defined until engineering selects the intended severity and identifies whether critical USB devices share the target controller.
